short: Improved mechanical and EMI shielding properties of PLA/PCL
title: Improved mechanical and EMI shielding properties of PLA/PCL composites by controlling distribution of PIL-modified CNTs

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: EMI shielding composites need high shielding with good mechanics from low filler loading. Steering PIL-modified CNTs to the PLA/PCL interface should raise both mechanics and EMI shielding.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/modification), n5 (DES/variable_sweep), n6 (PRC/forming)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: CNTs migrate from PLA to the interface and on into PCL with time; PIL holds them at the interface up to 6 min. PIL compatibilizes and widens the PLA/PCL interfacial layer.
states.detail: Absorbed: n7 (STR/microstructure/distribution), n9 (STR/interface), n8 (STR/microstructure/feature_size), n10 (STR/microstructure/distribution), n20 (STR/microstructure/distribution). Premises: Wetting coefficient 0.58 predicts thermodynamic CNT localization in PCL; PLA melt viscosity is ~16x that of PCL (Newtonian region); MEPGMA groups of PILs have high affinity for both PLA and PCL, raising compatibility [56]; A low-frequency G' plateau in a filled melt indicates a percolated filler network; Selective CNT localization at the interphase builds a more effective conductive network [63]

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Conductivity: PIL-free falls with blending time; PIL composites peak at 6 min (28.8 S/m) and exceed PIL-free ones. Elongation at break peaks at 6 min in both series (126% PIL-free, 135% PIL).
states.detail: Absorbed: n11 (PRP/value), n12 (PRP/value), n15 (MEC/pathway). Premises: In carbon-filled composites conduction loss dominates EMI shielding

states.title: Performance state
states.head: X-band EMI SE: PIL composites shield better, with PIL-6m highest at ~39-42 dB

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: PIL-modified CNTs localized at the PLA/PCL interface at 6 min blending give the best elongation, conductivity and absorption-dominated EMI SE

nodes.note: melting peaks near 55 and 166 C also stay put (moved from label at judge review). PIL series exotherm sits ~98 C vs ~96 C without PIL: not lower, although the text says PIL lowers Tcc; crystallinity (Table S2) not readable
